wallpapers.title: RED-EYED TREE FROG
wallpapers.line1: Agalychnis callidryas. Its eyes have no true eyelid, only a see-through membrane, so light still reaches them while it sleeps.
wallpapers.line2: 3 February 2011  ·  Photo: Brian Gratwicke (Flickr)  ·  CC BY 2.0

wallpapers.title: CHAMELEON EYE
wallpapers.line1: Its eyelids are joined, leaving only a pinhole for the pupil. Each eye turns and focuses on its own.
wallpapers.line2: 12 August 2009  ·  Photo: Umberto Salvagnin (Flickr)  ·  CC BY 2.0

wallpapers.title: GUMPRECHT'S GREEN PIT VIPER
wallpapers.line1: Trimeresurus gumprechti, a venomous female, Phu Suan Sai National Park, Thailand.

wallpapers.title: SMITH'S GREEN-EYED GECKO
wallpapers.line1: Gekko smithii, one of the biggest geckos, up to 35 cm long. Cameron Highlands, Malaysia.
wallpapers.line2: 18 April 2013  ·  Photo: Bernard Dupont (Flickr)  ·  CC BY-SA 2.0

wallpapers.title: EYELASH PIT VIPER
wallpapers.line1: Bothriechis nigroadspersus, the Central American eyelash pit viper, La Selva Biological Station, Costa Rica.
wallpapers.line2: 28 October 2011  ·  Photo: Geoff Gallice (Flickr)  ·  CC BY 2.0

wallpapers.title: WATER FROG EYE
wallpapers.line1: A green frog (Pelophylax) in the pond of the Düsseldorf Botanical Garden, Germany.
wallpapers.line2: 15 June 2022  ·  Photo: Carroll Diehl  ·  CC BY-SA 4.0

wallpapers.title: RETICULATED PYTHON
wallpapers.line1: Malayopython reticulatus, Kaeng Krachan, Thailand. Its mainland form is the world's longest snake.

wallpapers.title: DWARF CROCODILE
wallpapers.line1: Osteolaemus tetraspis, the smallest living crocodile, with a heavily armoured back. Karlsruhe Zoo, Germany.
wallpapers.line2: 19 August 2019  ·  Photo: H. Zell  ·  CC BY-SA 3.0

wallpapers.title: LARGE-EYED GREEN TREE SNAKE
wallpapers.line1: Rhamnophis aethiopissa at night in Korup National Park, Cameroon. It hunts frogs, lizards and birds in the trees.
wallpapers.line2: 26 January 2005  ·  Photo: Bernard Dupont (Flickr)  ·  CC BY-SA 2.0

wallpapers.title: INDIAN CHAMELEON
wallpapers.line1: Chamaeleo zeylanicus, its eye in its turret of scales. BNHS Conservation Education Centre, Mumbai, India.
wallpapers.line2: 22 June 2018  ·  Photo: Dr. Raju Kasambe  ·  CC BY-SA 4.0

wallpapers.title: CRAWFISH FROG
wallpapers.line1: Lithobates areolatus, Williamson County, Illinois. It lives in crayfish burrows for most of the year.
wallpapers.line2: 12 March 2021  ·  Photo: Peter Paplanus (Flickr)  ·  CC BY 2.0

wallpapers.title: AMERICAN CROCODILE
wallpapers.line1: Crocodylus acutus up close, La Manzanilla, Mexico. Besides the saltwater crocodile, the only crocodile that commonly lives in salt water.

wallpapers.title: GREEN-EYED BUSHFROG
wallpapers.line1: Raorchestes chlorosomma at Munnar in the southern Western Ghats, India.

wallpapers.title: BENGAL MONITOR
wallpapers.line1: Varanus bengalensis tasting the air with its forked tongue, Anawilundawa Bird Sanctuary, Sri Lanka.
wallpapers.line2: 19 February 2017  ·  Photo: Senthi Aathavan Senthilverl  ·  CC BY-SA 4.0
